qbiThreshold.label: Taxable income before the QBI deduction up to which Form 8995 is used

qbiThresholdJoint.label: Taxable income before the QBI deduction up to which Form 8995 is used, Married filing jointly
qbiThresholdJoint.source: Instructions, line 13a: $394,600 if married filing jointly

F8889.8.label: HSA contribution limit
F8889.8.formula: if(answer.hasHsa, if(answer.hsaAllYear == "yes", if(answer.hsaCoverage == "family", param.hsaFamily, param.hsaSelfOnly) + if(person.age >= 55, param.hsaCatchUp, 0), unsupported("HSA coverage for only part of 2025 is figured with the Line 3 Limitation Chart and the last-month rule, which this app doesn't work out")), 0)
F8889.8.source: Form 8889, lines 3 to 8: the limit for coverage all year, plus $1,000 at 55 or older; no Archer MSA

F8889.9.label: Employer contributions to your HSA
F8889.9.source: Form 8889, line 9: Form W-2, box 12, code W

F8889.13.label: HSA deduction
F8889.13.formula: if(line.F8889.2 + line.F8889.9 == 0, 0, if(line.F8889.2 + line.F8889.9 > line.F8889.8, unsupported("HSA contributions over the limit are an excess contribution (Form 5329), which this app doesn't work out"), if(answer.hsaNonMedical == "yes", unsupported("HSA distributions not for medical expenses are taxed on Form 8889, Part II, which this app doesn't prepare yet"), if(line.US.joint == 1 and answer.hsaCoverage == "family" and spouse.answer.hasHsa and spouse.answer.hsaCoverage == "family", unsupported("Both spouses with family HSA coverage share one limit, which this app doesn't split yet"), min(line.F8889.2, max(0, line.F8889.8 - line.F8889.9))))))
F8889.13.source: Form 8889, lines 10 to 13: the smaller of your contributions and the limit less employer contributions

S1.13.label: Health savings account deduction
S1.13.source: Schedule 1, line 13: Form 8889, line 13 (each spouse's on a joint return)

US.ownCompensation.label: This person's compensation for an IRA
US.ownCompensation.source: Instructions, IRA Deduction Worksheet, line 7: wages, plus self-employment income less the deductible part of self-employment tax

US.iraMagi.label: Modified AGI for the IRA deduction
US.iraMagi.formula: line.F1040.1z + line.F1040.2b + line.F1040.3b + line.F1040.4b + line.F1040.5b + line.F1040.7a + line.F1040.8 - line.S1.13 - line.S1.15
US.iraMagi.source: Instructions, IRA Deduction Worksheet, line 3: Form 1040 line 9 less Schedule 1 lines 11 to 19, 23 and 25, without the IRA and student loan interest deductions. Social security benefits are left out: with them, a phase-out is figured with Pub. 590-A, which this app doesn't do

US.iraPhaseOutStart.label: Where this person's IRA deduction starts to be reduced (0 if it isn't)
US.iraPhaseOutStart.formula: if(answer.coveredByPlan, if(line.US.joint == 1, param.iraPhaseOutJoint, if(line.US.separate == 1, 0, param.iraPhaseOutSingle)), if(line.US.joint == 1, if(spouse.answer.coveredByPlan, param.iraPhaseOutSpouseCovered, 0), 0))
US.iraPhaseOutStart.source: Instructions, IRA Deduction Worksheet, lines 1 and 2 (married filing separately and covered: from $0; a separate spouse who lived apart all year files as single, not worked out)

US.iraReduced.label: This person's IRA limit after the phase-out
US.iraReduced.formula: if(line.US.iraPhaseOutStart == 0 and line.US.separate == 0, line.US.iraLimit, if(line.US.separate == 0 and line.US.iraMagi <= line.US.iraPhaseOutStart, line.US.iraLimit, if(sum(SSA.box5) + if(line.US.joint == 1, sum(spouse.SSA.box5), 0) > 0, unsupported("With social security benefits and a retirement plan at work, the IRA deduction is figured with Pub. 590-A, which this app doesn't do"), if(line.US.iraMagi >= line.US.iraPhaseOutStart + if(line.US.joint == 1 and answer.coveredByPlan, param.iraPhaseOutRangeJoint, param.iraPhaseOutRange), 0, max(param.iraMinimum, 0 - floor(0 - line.US.iraLimit * (line.US.iraPhaseOutStart + if(line.US.joint == 1 and answer.coveredByPlan, param.iraPhaseOutRangeJoint, param.iraPhaseOutRange) - line.US.iraMagi) / if(line.US.joint == 1 and answer.coveredByPlan, param.iraPhaseOutRangeJoint, param.iraPhaseOutRange), 10))))))
US.iraReduced.source: Instructions, IRA Deduction Worksheet, lines 3 to 6: the limit times the part of the range left, rounded up to $10, and at least $200

US.ownIraDeduction.label: This person's IRA deduction
US.ownIraDeduction.formula: if(answer.hasIraContribution, min(answer.iraContribution, line.US.iraReduced, line.US.ownCompensation + if(line.US.joint == 1, max(0, spouse.line.US.ownCompensation - spouse.line.US.ownIraContribution), 0)), 0)
US.ownIraDeduction.source: Instructions, IRA Deduction Worksheet, lines 7 to 9: the smallest of the contributions, the limit and the compensation (with a spouse's, less their contributions, on a joint return)

US.ownPrivateActivityInterest.label: Specified private activity bond interest on this person's Forms 1099-INT (box 9) and 1099-DIV (box 13)

F6251.1a.label: Deductions less the enhanced deduction for seniors
F6251.1a.source: Form 6251, line 1a: Form 1040 line 14 less Schedule 1-A line 37

F6251.2a.label: Taxes, or the standard deduction
F6251.2a.source: Form 6251, line 2a: the taxes of Schedule A line 7; without Schedule A, Form 1040 line 12e

F6251.2g.label: Interest from specified private activity bonds
F6251.2g.source: 6251 instructions, line 2g: Form 1099-INT box 9 and Form 1099-DIV box 13

F6251.5.label: Exemption
F6251.5.formula: max(0, if(line.US.jointRates == 1, param.amtExemptionJoint, if(line.US.separate == 1, param.amtExemptionSeparate, param.amtExemptionSingle)) - round(max(0, line.F6251.4 - if(line.US.jointRates == 1, param.amtPhaseOutJoint, param.amtPhaseOutSingle)) * param.amtPhaseOutRate, 2))
F6251.5.source: Form 6251, line 5, and the Exemption Worksheet

F6251.39.label: Tentative tax on line 6 at the AMT rates
F6251.39.formula: round(if(line.F6251.6 <= if(line.US.separate == 1, param.amtBracketSeparate, param.amtBracket), line.F6251.6 * param.amtLowRate, line.F6251.6 * param.amtHighRate - if(line.US.separate == 1, param.amtBracketAdjustSeparate, param.amtBracketAdjust)), 2)

F6251.13.label: Qualified dividends and net capital gain
F6251.13.source: Form 6251, lines 13 to 15: line 4 of the Qualified Dividends and Capital Gain Tax Worksheet (no Schedule D Tax Worksheet, line 14 is 0)

F6251.17.label: AMTI taxed at the AMT rates

F6251.18.label: Tax on line 17 at the AMT rates
F6251.18.formula: round(if(line.F6251.17 <= if(line.US.separate == 1, param.amtBracketSeparate, param.amtBracket), line.F6251.17 * param.amtLowRate, line.F6251.17 * param.amtHighRate - if(line.US.separate == 1, param.amtBracketAdjustSeparate, param.amtBracketAdjust)), 2)

F6251.21.label: Room in the 0% band
F6251.21.source: Form 6251, lines 19 to 21: the 0% band less line 5 of the worksheet

F6251.40.label: Tentative tax with the capital gain rates
F6251.40.source: Form 6251, lines 38 to 40 (line 37 is 0 without unrecaptured section 1250 gain)

F6251.7.label: Tentative tax before the AMT foreign tax credit

F6251.10.label: Regular tax less the foreign tax credit
F6251.10.source: Form 6251, line 10: Form 1040 line 16 and Schedule 2 line 1z (none here), less Schedule 3 line 1

F6251.8.label: AMT foreign tax credit
F6251.8.source: 6251 instructions, line 8: with the foreign tax credit claimed without Form 1116, the same amount as Schedule 3 line 1

F1040.17.label: Alternative minimum tax (Schedule 2, line 3)
F1040.17.source: Schedule 2, lines 2 and 3: Form 6251, line 11 (no additions to tax on lines 1a to 1y)

DEP.livedWithYou.label: Lived with you more than half of 2025 (1 for yes)

DEP.careChild.label: A qualifying child under 13 for the care credit (1 for yes)
DEP.careChild.source: 2441 instructions, Qualifying Person(s), 1: a qualifying child under 13 you can claim; a child who turned 13 during 2025 qualifies for the part of the year before (the expenses asked are for that part)

DEP.careDependant.label: Your dependent, or would be but for their gross income or a joint return (1 for yes)
DEP.careDependant.formula: if(line.DEP.relatedChild == 1 and line.DEP.ageTest == 1 and not dependant.answer.paidOwnSupport and dependant.answer.citizenOrResident, 1, if(dependant.answer.relationship == "none" and dependant.answer.monthsWithYou < 12, 0, if(dependant.answer.supportedByYou and dependant.answer.citizenOrResident, 1, 0)))
DEP.careDependant.source: 2441 instructions, Qualifying Person(s), 3: a dependent, or one but for a gross income of $5,200 or more or a joint return

DEP.careDisabled.label: A dependant over 13 who can't care for themselves, for the care credit (1 for yes)
DEP.careDisabled.source: 2441 instructions, Qualifying Person(s), 3: not physically or mentally able to care for themselves, and lived with you more than half the year

DEP.careChildExpenses.label: Care expenses for a qualifying child under 13

DEP.careDisabledExpenses.label: Care expenses for a dependant who can't care for themselves

US.ownCareBenefits.label: Dependent care benefits on this person's Forms W-2, box 10
US.ownCareBenefits.formula: if(sum(W2.box10) > param.careBenefitsMax, unsupported("Dependent care benefits over $5,000 in box 10 of a W-2: the part over the plan's limit is already in box 1, which this app doesn't separate"), sum(W2.box10))
US.ownCareBenefits.source: 2441 instructions, line 12: box 10 of Form W-2, less amounts over the plan's exclusion that are reported as wages in box 1

US.careAsked.label: The return may have care expenses or dependent care benefits (1 for yes)
US.careAsked.source: 2441 instructions, Qualifying Person(s): a qualifying person lived with you more than half of 2025

US.paidForCare.label: You paid for care so you could work (1 for yes)

US.careUnmarried.label: Filing separately, treated as unmarried for the care credit (1 for yes)
US.careUnmarried.source: 2441 instructions, Married Persons Filing Separately: you lived apart from your spouse for the last 6 months of 2025 and paid more than half the cost of the home that was the qualifying person's main home for more than half the year (a qualifying person lived with you more than half the year in every case)

F2441.2.label: Qualifying persons
F2441.2.formula: if(line.US.paidForCare == 0, 0, if(line.US.claimsDependants == 1, sum(dependants.DEP.careChild), 0) + sum(dependants.DEP.careDisabled) + if(line.US.joint == 1, if(answer.spouseNeedsCare, unsupported("Care for your spouse, who couldn't care for themselves, isn't worked out by this app yet (Form 2441)"), 0), 0))
F2441.2.source: Form 2441, line 2: a qualifying child under 13 needs you to be able to claim dependants; someone who can't care for themselves counts even when you could be claimed yourself (2441 instructions, Qualifying Person(s), 3c)

US.careExpenses.label: Care expenses for the qualifying persons
US.careExpenses.source: Form 2441, line 2, column (d), before the benefits of Part III are taken off (line 30)

US.careDeemedMonthly.label: Earned income treated as earned for each month as a student or not able to care for oneself

US.careEarnedSelf.label: Your earned income for Form 2441, without dependent care benefits
US.careEarnedSelf.formula: if(line.US.joint == 0, line.US.ownEarned, if(answer.studentOrDisabledMonths == 0, line.US.ownEarned, if(line.US.ownEarned > 0, unsupported("You had wages in months you were a student or weren't able to care for yourself: Form 2441 then compares them month by month, which this app doesn't do"), if(spouse.answer.studentOrDisabledMonths > 0, unsupported("You and your spouse were both students or not able to care for yourselves in 2025: Form 2441 counts only one of you in a month, which this app doesn't work out"), answer.studentOrDisabledMonths * line.US.careDeemedMonthly))))
US.careEarnedSelf.source: 2441 instructions, lines 4 and 5, If You or Your Spouse Was a Student or Disabled

US.careEarnedSpouse.label: Your spouse's earned income for Form 2441, without dependent care benefits
US.careEarnedSpouse.formula: if(spouse.answer.studentOrDisabledMonths == 0, spouse.line.US.ownEarned, if(spouse.line.US.ownEarned > 0, unsupported("Your spouse had wages in months they were a student or weren't able to care for themselves: Form 2441 then compares them month by month, which this app doesn't do"), if(answer.studentOrDisabledMonths > 0, unsupported("You and your spouse were both students or not able to care for yourselves in 2025: Form 2441 counts only one of you in a month, which this app doesn't work out"), spouse.answer.studentOrDisabledMonths * line.US.careDeemedMonthly)))
US.careEarnedSpouse.source: 2441 instructions, lines 4 and 5, If You or Your Spouse Was a Student or Disabled

US.careTaxableSelf.label: Your part of the taxable dependent care benefits
US.careTaxableSelf.formula: if(line.US.joint == 0, line.F2441.26, if(line.F2441.12 == 0, 0, round(line.F2441.26 * line.US.ownCareBenefits / line.F2441.12, 2)))
US.careTaxableSelf.source: Form 1040, line 1e is earned income (line 1z); filing jointly, it is shared by each spouse's box 10

F2441.12.label: Dependent care benefits received
F2441.12.source: Form 2441, line 12: box 10 of each Form W-2 (both spouses' filing jointly)

F2441.13.label: Benefits carried over from 2024 and used in the grace period

F2441.14.label: Benefits forfeited or carried forward to 2026

F2441.15.label: Benefits for 2025
F2441.15.source: Form 2441, line 15: lines 12 and 13, less line 14

F2441.17.label: The smaller of line 15 and line 16

F2441.18.label: Your earned income
F2441.18.source: 2441 instructions, line 18: as for line 4, but without the dependent care benefits on line 12

F2441.19.label: Your spouse's earned income, or yours
F2441.19.formula: if(line.US.joint == 1, line.US.careEarnedSpouse, if(line.US.separate == 1, if(line.US.careUnmarried == 1, line.F2441.18, spouse.line.US.ownEarned), line.F2441.18))
F2441.19.source: 2441 instructions, line 19: filing separately and not treated as unmarried, your spouse's earned income

F2441.21.label: Most benefits that can be excluded
F2441.21.source: Form 2441, line 21: $5,000; $2,500 filing separately with the spouse's earned income on line 19. A plan with a lower limit isn't asked about

F2441.25.label: Excluded benefits
F2441.25.source: Form 2441, lines 22 to 25: no benefits from a sole proprietorship or partnership (line 22 is 0), so none are deductible (line 24). With no benefits, the earned income of lines 18 and 19 isn't needed

F2441.26.label: Taxable benefits
F2441.26.source: Form 2441, lines 23 and 26: line 15 less the excluded benefits; it goes on Form 1040, line 1e

F2441.29.label: Most expenses left after the excluded benefits
F2441.29.source: Form 2441, lines 28 and 29: line 27 less the deductible (none) and excluded benefits

F2441.30.label: Expenses not paid with excluded benefits
F2441.30.source: Form 2441, line 30: line 2, column (d), without the benefits on line 28

F2441.31.label: Expenses for the credit after the benefits

F2441.3.label: Expenses for the credit
F2441.3.source: Form 2441, line 3: line 2, column (d), up to $3,000 ($6,000); line 31 when Part III is completed

F2441.4.label: Your earned income
F2441.4.source: 2441 instructions, lines 4 and 5: Form 1040 line 1z, figured for each spouse filing jointly

F2441.5.label: Your spouse's earned income, or yours

F2441.8.label: Credit rate
F2441.8.formula: max(param.careRateMin, param.careRateMax - param.careRateStep * max(0, 0 - floor(param.careRateStart - line.F2441.7, 2000)) / 2000)
F2441.8.source: Form 2441, line 8: .35 up to $15,000, then .01 less for each $2,000 (or part of it) over, down to .20 over $43,000

F2441.10.label: Tax liability limit
F2441.10.source: 2441 instructions, Credit Limit Worksheet: Form 1040 line 18, less Schedule 3 lines 1 (the foreign tax credit, investments.yaml) and 6l (not worked out by this app)

F2441.11.label: Credit for child and dependent care expenses
F2441.11.source: Form 2441, line 11: the smaller of lines 9c and 10; none without care expenses (line 3 is then 0). Line 9b, for 2024 care paid in 2025, is 0 (SCOPE.care says when it isn't). Filing separately, only when treated as unmarried (2441 instructions, line A)

S3.2.label: Credit for child and dependent care expenses

S3.8.label: Total nonrefundable credits from Schedule 3
S3.8.source: Schedule 3, line 8: lines 1 (investments.yaml), 2 and 3 (education.yaml); no other nonrefundable credit is worked out by this app

SCOPE.care.label: Care this app doesn't handle yet
SCOPE.care.formula: if(line.US.paidForCare == 0, 0, if(answer.householdEmployer, unsupported("Household employment taxes for a household employee (Schedule H) aren't worked out by this app"), 0) + if(answer.priorYearCare, unsupported("Care given in 2024 and paid for in 2025 adds to the credit on Form 2441 line 9b (Worksheet A), which this app doesn't work out yet"), 0))
SCOPE.care.source: Instructions for Schedule H (2025), lines A to C: cash wages of $2,800 to one employee, or $1,000 in a calendar quarter; 2441 instructions, line 9b and Worksheet A

DEP.relatedChild.label: Related as a qualifying child can be (1 for yes)
DEP.relatedChild.formula: if(dependant.answer.relationship == "child" or dependant.answer.relationship == "foster" or dependant.answer.relationship == "sibling" or dependant.answer.relationship == "descendant", 1, 0)
DEP.relatedChild.source: Instructions, Qualifying child: your son, daughter, stepchild, foster child, brother, sister, or a descendant of any of them

DEP.ageTest.label: Meets the qualifying child's age test (1 for yes)
DEP.ageTest.source: Instructions, Qualifying child: under 19 at the end of 2025, or under 24 and a full-time student, or any age and permanently and totally disabled

DEP.qualifyingChild.label: A qualifying child (1 for yes)
DEP.qualifyingChild.formula: if(line.DEP.relatedChild == 1 and dependant.answer.monthsWithYou >= 7 and line.DEP.ageTest == 1 and not dependant.answer.paidOwnSupport and not dependant.answer.filedJointReturn and dependant.answer.citizenOrResident, 1, 0)
DEP.qualifyingChild.source: Instructions, Who Qualifies as Your Dependent: lived with you more than half of 2025, didn't pay over half of their own support, files no joint return

DEP.qualifyingRelative.label: A qualifying relative (1 for yes)
DEP.qualifyingRelative.formula: if(line.DEP.qualifyingChild == 1, 0, if(dependant.answer.relationship == "none" and dependant.answer.monthsWithYou < 12, 0, if(dependant.answer.grossIncome < param.relativeIncomeLimit and dependant.answer.supportedByYou and dependant.answer.citizenOrResident and not dependant.answer.filedJointReturn, 1, 0)))
DEP.qualifyingRelative.source: Instructions, Qualifying relative: related to you or lived with you all year, gross income under $5,200, and you paid over half of their support

DEP.ctcChild.label: A qualifying child for the child tax credit (1 for yes)
DEP.ctcChild.source: 8812 instructions: a qualifying child under 17 at the end of 2025 with a social security number valid for employment

DEP.hohQualifying.label: Lets you file as head of household (1 for yes)
DEP.hohQualifying.source: Instructions, Head of Household: a qualifying child, a related qualifying relative who lived with you more than half the year, or a parent who didn't have to live with you

DEP.qssChild.label: Lets a widow or widower file as a qualifying surviving spouse (1 for yes)
DEP.qssChild.source: Instructions, Qualifying Surviving Spouse: a child or stepchild (not a foster child) you can claim, who lived in your home all year

US.claimsDependants.label: This return can claim dependants (1 for yes)
US.claimsDependants.source: Instructions, Dependents: if someone can claim you (or your spouse on a joint return) as a dependent, you can't claim anyone

US.filerSSN.label: You, or your spouse on a joint return, have a social security number valid for employment (1 for yes)
US.filerSSN.source: 8812 instructions: from 2025 you need a valid SSN to claim the CTC or ACTC; filing jointly, one spouse's is enough

S8812.3.label: Modified adjusted gross income
S8812.3.source: Schedule 8812, line 3: line 11b, plus income excluded from Puerto Rico or abroad (not handled)

S8812.4.label: Qualifying children for the child tax credit

S8812.5.label: Child tax credit before the reduction

S8812.6.label: Other dependents
S8812.6.source: Schedule 8812, line 6: each dependent who isn't counted on line 4, including a child the CTC can't be claimed for without a valid SSN

S8812.7.label: Credit for other dependents before the reduction

S8812.8.label: Child tax credit and credit for other dependents

S8812.9.label: Modified AGI over which the credits are reduced

S8812.10.label: Modified AGI over the threshold, rounded up to the next $1,000
S8812.10.source: Schedule 8812, line 10: line 3 less line 9; more than zero and not a multiple of $1,000, the next multiple of $1,000

S8812.13.label: Credit limit
S8812.13.source: 8812 instructions, Credit Limit Worksheet A: Form 1040 line 18, less Schedule 3 lines 1 to 3 (the foreign tax credit and the credits for child and dependent care expenses and for education); the other credits it lists aren't worked out by this app

S8812.14.label: Child tax credit and credit for other dependents

S8812.17.label: The smaller of line 16a and line 16b

S8812.18a.label: Earned income
S8812.18a.source: 8812 instructions, Earned Income Chart and Earned Income Worksheet: wages on Form 1040 line 1z, plus a net profit from self-employment less the deductible part of its tax (no nontaxable combat pay)

US.ownSocialAndMedicare.label: Social security and Medicare tax withheld on this person's Forms W-2

S8812.21.label: Social security, Medicare and Additional Medicare tax withheld
S8812.21.source: Schedule 8812, line 21: Forms W-2, boxes 4 and 6 (both spouses' on a joint return)

S8812.22.label: Deductible part of self-employment tax
S8812.22.source: Schedule 8812, line 22: Schedule 1, line 15 (no Schedule 2, lines 5, 6 or 13)

S8812.23.label: Taxes withheld and self-employment tax deducted

S8812.24.label: Earned income credit and excess social security tax
S8812.24.source: Schedule 8812, line 24: Form 1040 line 27a and Schedule 3 line 11

S8812.25.label: Taxes withheld over the earned income credit

S8812.26.label: The larger of line 20 and line 25

S8812.27.formula: if(line.S8812.16a == 0, 0, if(line.S8812.16b >= param.actcThreeChildren, min(line.S8812.17, line.S8812.26), min(line.S8812.17, line.S8812.20)))
S8812.27.source: Schedule 8812, lines 16a to 27: Part II-B when line 16b is $5,100 or more (three or more children)

US.educationAllowed.label: This return can take the education credits and the student loan interest deduction (1 for yes)
US.educationAllowed.source: 8863 instructions, Who Can Claim an Education Credit: not married filing separately, and not someone listed as a dependent on another's return; Instructions, Schedule 1, line 21: the same for the student loan interest deduction

US.educationAsked.label: You, or your spouse on a joint return, paid for higher education (1 for yes)

US.ownStudentExpenses.label: This person's own adjusted qualified education expenses
US.ownStudentExpenses.source: 8863 instructions, Adjusted Qualified Education Expenses Worksheet: expenses paid in 2025, less tax-free educational assistance

US.tuitionStatements.label: Payments on this person's Forms 1098-T, less scholarships and refunds
US.tuitionStatements.source: 8863 instructions, Qualified Education Expenses: you may get a Form 1098-T; reduce the expenses by tax-free educational assistance and refunds

US.ownAotcStudent.label: This person takes the American opportunity credit (1 for yes)
US.ownAotcStudent.source: Form 8863, lines 23 to 26: the student meets each condition

US.ownAotc27.label: This person's expenses for the American opportunity credit, up to $4,000

US.ownAotc30.label: This person's American opportunity credit before the limits
US.ownAotc30.formula: min(line.US.ownAotc27, param.aotcFullRate) + round(max(0, line.US.ownAotc27 - param.aotcFullRate) * param.aotcPartRate, 2)
US.ownAotc30.source: Form 8863, lines 28 to 30: line 27, up to $2,000, plus 25% of the rest

US.ownLlc31.label: This person's expenses for the lifetime learning credit
US.ownLlc31.source: Form 8863, line 31: not for a student who takes the American opportunity credit

DEP.studentExpenses.source: 8863 instructions, Who Can Claim an Education Credit: expenses for a dependent you claim, paid by you or by the dependent. They aren't asked for a child under 14 at the end of 2025, who isn't likely to be in college

DEP.aotcStudent.label: This dependant takes the American opportunity credit (1 for yes)

DEP.aotc27.label: Expenses for the American opportunity credit, up to $4,000

DEP.llc31.label: Expenses for the lifetime learning credit for this dependant

F8863.1.label: American opportunity credit before the income limit
F8863.1.source: Form 8863, line 1: each student's Part III, line 30

F8863.2.label: Modified AGI from which there is no credit

F8863.3.source: 8863 instructions, line 3: Form 1040, line 11b (no income excluded from Puerto Rico or abroad)

F8863.6.source: Form 8863, line 6: 1.000, or line 4 divided by line 5 as a decimal rounded to three places

F8863.7.label: American opportunity credit after the income limit

US.aotcNoRefund.label: None of the American opportunity credit is refundable (1 for yes)
US.aotcNoRefund.formula: if(line.US.joint == 1, 0, if(person.age >= 24, 0, if(line.F8863.7 == 0, 0, if(answer.parentAlive, if(person.age < 18, 1, if(person.age == 18, if(answer.earnedUnderHalfSupport, 1, 0), if(answer.fullTimeStudentSelf, if(answer.earnedUnderHalfSupport, 1, 0), 0))), 0))))
US.aotcNoRefund.source: 8863 instructions, line 7: you were under 18; or 18, or a full-time student under 24, with earned income less than half of your support; at least one of your parents was alive at the end of 2025; and you aren't filing jointly. The age is the year less the birth year

F8863.8.label: Refundable American opportunity credit
F8863.8.source: Form 8863, line 8: 40% of line 7, on Form 1040, line 29

F8863.10.label: Expenses for the lifetime learning credit
F8863.10.source: Form 8863, line 10: each student's Part III, line 31

F8863.11.label: Expenses for the lifetime learning credit, up to $10,000

F8863.12.label: Lifetime learning credit before the income limit

F8863.15.label: Modified AGI under the limit, for the lifetime learning credit
F8863.15.source: Form 8863, lines 13 to 15: the same as lines 2 to 4

F8863.17.label: Share of the lifetime learning credit allowed
F8863.17.source: Form 8863, lines 16 and 17: as lines 5 and 6

F8863.19.label: Nonrefundable education credits
F8863.19.formula: min(line.F8863.18 + line.F8863.9, max(0, line.F1040.18 - line.S3.1 - line.S3.2))
F8863.19.source: 8863 instructions, Credit Limit Worksheet: lines 18 and 9, up to Form 1040 line 18 less Schedule 3 lines 1, 2, 6d and 6l (only line 2, the credit for child and dependent care expenses, is worked out by this app)

US.ownStudentLoan.label: Student loan interest this person paid
US.ownStudentLoan.formula: if(answer.hasStudentLoan, answer.studentLoanInterest + sum(F1098E.box1), if(count(F1098E.box1) > 0, unsupported("A Form 1098-E is added, but no student loan interest: say you paid it on Deductions, or remove the 1098-E"), 0))

SLW.1.label: Student loan interest, up to $2,500
SLW.1.source: Student Loan Interest Deduction Worksheet, line 1: $2,500 for the return, filing jointly too

SLW.4.label: Modified adjusted gross income
SLW.4.source: Student Loan Interest Deduction Worksheet, lines 2 to 4: Form 1040 line 9, less Schedule 1 lines 11 to 20, 23 and 25 (only line 15 is worked out by this app)

SLW.5.label: Modified AGI over which the deduction is reduced

SLW.7.label: Share of the interest not deducted
SLW.7.source: Student Loan Interest Deduction Worksheet, line 7: line 6 divided by $15,000 ($30,000 jointly), rounded to three places, 1.000 at most

S1.21.label: Student loan interest deduction
S1.21.source: Student Loan Interest Deduction Worksheet, line 9: line 1 less line 8; not filing separately, or when someone can claim you

DEP.eicChild.label: A qualifying child for the earned income credit (1 for yes)
DEP.eicChild.formula: if(line.DEP.relatedChild == 1 and dependant.answer.monthsWithYou >= 7 and line.DEP.ageTest == 1 and not dependant.answer.filedJointReturn, if(dependant.answer.hasSSN, 1, 0), 0)
DEP.eicChild.source: Instructions, line 27a, Step 3, Qualifying Child, with a valid SSN (Step 1)

US.eicChildren.label: Qualifying children for the earned income credit

US.eicKids.label: Qualifying children counted for the EIC Table (three or more count as three)

US.eicRateIn.label: Earned income credit rate as it rises
US.eicRateIn.formula: if(line.US.eicKids == 0, param.eicRateInNoChild, if(line.US.eicKids == 1, param.eicRateInOneChild, if(line.US.eicKids == 2, param.eicRateInTwoChildren, param.eicRateInThreeChildren)))

US.eicMax.label: Largest earned income credit
US.eicMax.formula: if(line.US.eicKids == 0, param.eicMaxNoChild, if(line.US.eicKids == 1, param.eicMaxOneChild, if(line.US.eicKids == 2, param.eicMaxTwoChildren, param.eicMaxThreeChildren)))

US.eicEarnedAmount.label: Earned income at which the credit is largest
US.eicEarnedAmount.formula: if(line.US.eicKids == 0, param.eicEarnedAmountNoChild, if(line.US.eicKids == 1, param.eicEarnedAmountOneChild, if(line.US.eicKids == 2, param.eicEarnedAmountTwoChildren, param.eicEarnedAmountThreeChildren)))

US.eicRateOut.label: Earned income credit phase-out rate
US.eicRateOut.formula: if(line.US.eicKids == 0, param.eicRateOutNoChild, if(line.US.eicKids == 1, param.eicRateOutOneChild, if(line.US.eicKids == 2, param.eicRateOutTwoChildren, param.eicRateOutThreeChildren)))

US.eicStart.label: Income from which the earned income credit goes down
US.eicStart.formula: if(line.US.eicKids == 0, if(line.US.joint == 1, param.eicStartNoChildJoint, param.eicStartNoChild), if(line.US.eicKids == 1, if(line.US.joint == 1, param.eicStartOneChildJoint, param.eicStartOneChild), if(line.US.eicKids == 2, if(line.US.joint == 1, param.eicStartTwoChildrenJoint, param.eicStartTwoChildren), if(line.US.joint == 1, param.eicStartThreeChildrenJoint, param.eicStartThreeChildren))))

US.eicLimit.label: Income from which there is no earned income credit
US.eicLimit.formula: if(line.US.eicKids == 0, if(line.US.joint == 1, param.eicLimitNoChildJoint, param.eicLimitNoChild), if(line.US.eicKids == 1, if(line.US.joint == 1, param.eicLimitOneChildJoint, param.eicLimitOneChild), if(line.US.eicKids == 2, if(line.US.joint == 1, param.eicLimitTwoChildrenJoint, param.eicLimitTwoChildren), if(line.US.joint == 1, param.eicLimitThreeChildrenJoint, param.eicLimitThreeChildren))))

US.eicAge.label: People on the return 25 to 64 at the end of 2025
US.eicAge.formula: if(person.age >= 25 and person.age < 65, 1, 0) + if(line.US.joint == 1, if(spouse.person.age >= 25 and spouse.person.age < 65, 1, 0), 0)
US.eicAge.source: Instructions, line 27a, Step 4: at least 25 but under 65 at the end of 2025 (you, or your spouse filing jointly)

US.eicSSN.label: You, and your spouse filing jointly, have a valid SSN (1 for yes)

US.eicEligible.label: Can take the earned income credit (1 for yes)
US.eicEligible.formula: if(line.US.claimable == 1, 0, if(line.US.earnedIncome < 1, 0, if(line.F1040.2a + line.F1040.2b + line.F1040.3b + max(0, line.F1040.7a) > param.eicInvestmentLimit, 0, if(line.F1040.11a >= line.US.eicLimit or line.US.earnedIncome >= line.US.eicLimit, 0, if(line.US.eicKids == 0, if(line.US.separate == 1 or line.US.hoh == 1, 0, if(line.US.eicAge > 0, line.US.eicSSN, 0)), if(line.US.separate == 1, if(answer.livedApartLastSixMonths, line.US.eicSSN, 0), line.US.eicSSN))))))
US.eicEligible.source: Instructions, line 27a: Step 1 (AGI under the limit, valid SSNs), Step 2 (investment income: lines 2a, 2b and 3b, and line 7a when a gain), Step 3 (filing separately: a qualifying child and living apart for the last 6 months; not someone else's qualifying child, which the app takes as not being someone's dependent), Step 4 (no qualifying child: 25 to 64, not separately or head of household) and Step 5 (earned income under the limit)

US.eicRowEarned.label: Start of the EIC Table's row for earned income

US.eicRowEndEarned.label: End of the EIC Table's row for earned income; the last row of a column stops at the limit

US.eicMiddleEarned.label: Middle of the EIC Table's row for earned income

US.eicTableEarned.label: Earned income credit from the EIC Table for earned income
US.eicTableEarned.formula: if(line.US.earnedIncome < 1 or line.US.earnedIncome >= line.US.eicLimit, 0, round(max(0, if(line.US.eicRowEndEarned > line.US.eicEarnedAmount, line.US.eicMax, min(line.US.eicRateIn * line.US.eicMiddleEarned, line.US.eicMax)) - if(line.US.eicRowEarned >= line.US.eicStart, line.US.eicRateOut * (line.US.eicMiddleEarned - line.US.eicStart), 0)), 0))
US.eicTableEarned.source: The 2025 EIC Table (Instructions, pages 49 to 60), checked row by row: each row's credit is worked out on the middle of the row (of the narrower last row, by its limit), to the nearest dollar; the row with the earned income amount gives the largest credit, and it goes down only from rows starting at the phase-out start

US.eicRowAGI.label: Start of the EIC Table's row for adjusted gross income

US.eicRowEndAGI.label: End of the EIC Table's row for adjusted gross income; the last row of a column stops at the limit

US.eicMiddleAGI.label: Middle of the EIC Table's row for adjusted gross income

US.eicTableAGI.label: Earned income credit from the EIC Table for adjusted gross income
US.eicTableAGI.formula: if(line.F1040.11a < 1 or line.F1040.11a >= line.US.eicLimit, 0, round(max(0, if(line.US.eicRowEndAGI > line.US.eicEarnedAmount, line.US.eicMax, min(line.US.eicRateIn * line.US.eicMiddleAGI, line.US.eicMax)) - if(line.US.eicRowAGI >= line.US.eicStart, line.US.eicRateOut * (line.US.eicMiddleAGI - line.US.eicStart), 0)), 0))
US.eicTableAGI.source: The 2025 EIC Table (Instructions, pages 49 to 60), checked row by row: each row's credit is worked out on the middle of the row (of the narrower last row, by its limit), to the nearest dollar; the row with the earned income amount gives the largest credit, and it goes down only from rows starting at the phase-out start

F1040.27a.label: Earned income credit
F1040.27a.formula: if(line.US.eicEligible == 0, 0, if(line.F1040.11a == line.US.earnedIncome or line.F1040.11a < line.US.eicStart, line.US.eicTableEarned, min(line.US.eicTableEarned, line.US.eicTableAGI)))
F1040.27a.source: Instructions, EIC Worksheet A: the credit on earned income; when AGI differs and isn't under the phase-out start, the smaller of that and the credit on AGI

US.single.label: Filing status is Single (1 for yes)

US.hoh.label: Filing status is Head of household (1 for yes)
US.hoh.source: Instructions, Head of Household: unmarried, paid over half the cost of keeping up a home, with a qualifying person; it is never worse than Single

US.qss.label: Filing status is Qualifying surviving spouse (1 for yes)
US.qss.formula: if(family.maritalStatus == "widowed", if(answer.spouseDiedIn2025, 0, if(answer.spouseDiedIn2023Or2024, if(line.US.claimsDependants == 0, 0, if(sum(dependants.DEP.qssChild) == 0, 0, if(answer.paidHalfOfHome, 1, 0))), 0)), 0)
US.qss.source: Instructions, Qualifying Surviving Spouse: spouse died in 2023 or 2024, a dependent child who lived with you all year, and you paid over half the cost of the home

US.jointRates.label: Joint return rates, Married filing jointly or Qualifying surviving spouse (1 for yes)

US.joint.label: Filing status is Married filing jointly (1 for yes)

US.separate.label: Filing status is Married filing separately (1 for yes)

US.ownWages.label: Wages on this person's Forms W-2, box 1

US.ownTaxableInterest.label: This person's taxable interest, Forms 1099-INT boxes 1 and 3

US.ownExemptInterest.label: This person's tax-exempt interest, Forms 1099-INT box 8 and 1099-DIV box 12

US.ownMedicareWages.label: This person's Medicare wages and tips, Forms W-2 box 5

US.ownMedicareTax.label: This person's Medicare tax withheld, Forms W-2 box 6

US.ownWithheldW2.label: Federal income tax withheld on this person's Forms W-2

US.ownWithheld1099.label: Federal income tax withheld on this person's Forms 1099
US.ownWithheld1099.formula: sum(INT.box4) + sum(NEC.box4) + sum(DIV.box4) + sum(B.box4) + sum(RIRA.box4) + sum(R.box4) + sum(SSA.box6)

US.ownBoxes.label: This person's boxes on line 12d (born before January 2, 1961; blind)
US.ownBoxes.source: Form 1040, line 12d. Someone born on January 1, 1961 counts as 65 for 2025; the app knows the birth year only and counts them as 64. On a separate return the spouse's boxes, which count only when the spouse had no income and files no return, aren't counted

US.ownExcessSocialSecurity.label: Social security tax withheld on this person's wages over the 2025 maximum
US.ownExcessSocialSecurity.formula: if(max(W2.box4) > param.socialSecurityMax, unsupported("An employer withheld more social security tax than the 2025 maximum of $10,918.20; ask it to refund the excess"), if(countIssuers(W2.box4) > 1, max(0, sum(W2.box4) - param.socialSecurityMax), 0))
US.ownExcessSocialSecurity.source: Instructions, Schedule 3, line 11: with more than one employer, the tax withheld over $10,918.20, figured separately for you and your spouse

F1040.2a.label: Tax-exempt interest
F1040.2a.source: Form 1040, line 2a: Form 1099-INT, box 8, and Form 1099-DIV, box 12. It isn't taxed; it is reported

F1040.2b.label: Taxable interest
F1040.2b.source: Form 1040, line 2b: Form 1099-INT, boxes 1 and 3 (savings bond and Treasury interest is taxed federally)

F1040.9.label: Total income
F1040.9.formula: line.F1040.1z + line.F1040.2b + line.F1040.3b + line.F1040.4b + line.F1040.5b + line.F1040.6b + line.F1040.7a + line.F1040.8

US.earnedIncome.label: Earned income
US.earnedIncome.source: Instructions, line 27a, Worksheet B, and the Standard Deduction Worksheet for Dependents: wages (line 1z) plus the net profit from self-employment, less the deductible part of self-employment tax (Schedule 1, line 15)

US.claimable.label: Someone can claim you, or your spouse on a joint return, as a dependent (1 for yes)

US.basicStandard.label: Standard deduction for the filing status
US.basicStandard.formula: if(line.US.jointRates == 1, param.standardJoint, if(line.US.hoh == 1, param.standardHead, if(line.US.single == 1, param.standardSingle, param.standardSeparate)))

US.dependentStandard.label: Standard deduction for someone who can be claimed as a dependent, before line 12d's boxes
US.dependentStandard.source: Instructions, Standard Deduction Worksheet for Dependents, lines 2 to 4

US.standard.label: Standard deduction with line 12d's boxes
US.standard.formula: if(line.US.claimable == 1, line.US.dependentStandard, line.US.basicStandard) + line.US.boxes * if(line.US.single == 1 or line.US.hoh == 1, param.additionalUnmarried, param.additionalMarried)

F1040.12e.label: Standard deduction or itemized deductions
F1040.12e.source: Form 1040, line 12e: the standard deduction, or itemized deductions from Schedule A (itemized.yaml)

S1A.3.label: Modified adjusted gross income
S1A.3.source: Schedule 1-A, line 3: line 11b, plus income excluded from Puerto Rico or abroad (not handled)

S1A.32.label: Modified AGI over which the deduction is reduced

S1A.35.label: Enhanced deduction for seniors, after the reduction
S1A.35.formula: max(0, param.seniorAmount - round(max(0, line.S1A.3 - line.S1A.32) * param.seniorPhaseOutRate, 2))

S1A.37.label: Enhanced deduction for seniors
S1A.37.formula: if(line.US.separate == 1, 0, if(person.age >= 65, line.S1A.35, 0) + if(line.US.joint == 1, if(spouse.person.age >= 65, line.S1A.35, 0), 0))
S1A.37.source: Schedule 1-A, lines 36a and 36b: you, and your spouse on a joint return, born before January 2, 1961, with a valid social security number

F1040.13b.label: Additional deductions from Schedule 1-A
F1040.13b.source: Schedule 1-A, line 38: the deductions for qualified tips, overtime and car loan interest (schedule1a.yaml) and for seniors

US.tableRow.label: The middle of the Tax Table's row for line 15
US.tableRow.source: 2025 Tax Table: rows of $5, $10 and $10, then $25 wide to $3,000 and $50 wide to $100,000. Each row's tax is the tax on the middle of the row, to the nearest dollar ($3,000 to $3,050: $303)

US.tableTax.label: Tax from the Tax Table
US.tableTax.formula: round(if(line.US.jointRates == 1, bracket(param.bracketsJoint, line.US.tableRow), if(line.US.hoh == 1, bracket(param.bracketsHead, line.US.tableRow), if(line.US.single == 1, bracket(param.bracketsSingle, line.US.tableRow), bracket(param.bracketsSeparate, line.US.tableRow)))), 0)

US.worksheetTax.label: Tax from the Tax Computation Worksheet
US.worksheetTax.formula: round(if(line.US.jointRates == 1, bracket(param.bracketsJoint, line.F1040.15), if(line.US.hoh == 1, bracket(param.bracketsHead, line.F1040.15), if(line.US.single == 1, bracket(param.bracketsSingle, line.F1040.15), bracket(param.bracketsSeparate, line.F1040.15)))), 2)

US.regularTax.label: Tax on taxable income at the regular rates

F1040.16.label: Tax
F1040.16.source: Instructions, line 16: the Tax Table under $100,000, the Tax Computation Worksheet from $100,000, or the Qualified Dividends and Capital Gain Tax Worksheet (investments.yaml) with qualified dividends or capital gains

F1040.18.label: Tax and the alternative minimum tax

F1040.19.label: Child tax credit and credit for other dependents

F8959.1.label: Medicare wages and tips
F8959.1.source: Form 8959, line 1: Form W-2, box 5 (both spouses' on a joint return)

F8959.5.label: Threshold for Additional Medicare Tax
F8959.5.source: Instructions, Schedule 2, line 11: $200,000 for single, head of household or qualifying surviving spouse

F8959.7.label: Additional Medicare Tax on Medicare wages

F8959.8.label: Self-employment income for Additional Medicare Tax
F8959.8.source: Form 8959, line 8: Schedule SE, Part I, line 6 (both spouses' on a joint return)

F8959.11.label: Threshold left after Medicare wages
F8959.11.source: Form 8959, lines 9 to 11: the line 5 threshold less the Medicare wages of line 4

F8959.13.label: Additional Medicare Tax on self-employment income

F8959.18.label: Total Additional Medicare Tax
F8959.18.source: Form 8959, line 18: lines 7 and 13 (no railroad retirement compensation, line 17)

F8960.8.label: Total investment income
F8960.8.source: Form 8960, lines 1, 2, 5a and 8: taxable interest, ordinary dividends, and the net gain or loss of Form 1040 line 7a; no annuities, rents or business income here

F8960.12.label: Net investment income
F8960.12.source: Form 8960, line 12: line 8 less the deductions of lines 9 to 11 (none worked out); if zero or less, 0

F8960.14.label: Threshold for the net investment income tax
F8960.14.source: Instructions, Schedule 2, line 12: $250,000 married filing jointly or qualifying surviving spouse; $200,000 single or head of household

F8960.17.label: Net investment income tax
F8960.17.source: Form 8960, lines 13 to 17: the smaller of the net investment income and the MAGI over the threshold, times 3.8%

S2.4.label: Self-employment tax
S2.4.source: Schedule 2, line 4: Schedule SE, line 12 (each spouse's on a joint return)

S2.21.label: Total other taxes
S2.21.source: Schedule 2, line 21: lines 4 (Schedule SE), 8 (the 10% tax on early distributions, retirement.yaml), 11 (Form 8959) and 12 (Form 8960)

F1040.25a.label: Federal income tax withheld on Forms W-2

F1040.25b.label: Federal income tax withheld on Forms 1099

F8959.21.label: Regular Medicare tax withholding on Medicare wages

F8959.24.label: Additional Medicare Tax withheld
F8959.24.source: Form 8959, lines 19 to 24: what box 6 holds above 1.45% of box 5

F1040.25c.label: Federal income tax withheld on other forms
F1040.25c.source: Instructions, line 25c: the Additional Medicare Tax withheld, Form 8959 line 24

S3.11.label: Excess social security tax withheld
S3.11.source: Instructions, Schedule 3, line 11: figured separately for you and your spouse, then added

F1040.34.label: Refund
F1040.34.source: Form 1040, line 34: the amount you overpaid

RESULT.net.label: Refund, less the amount owed
RESULT.net.source: On a joint return the spouse has no refund or amount owed of their own: hints add this line over both returns

SCOPE.return.label: Situations this app doesn't handle yet
SCOPE.return.formula: line.SCOPE.residency + line.SCOPE.widowed + line.SCOPE.kiddie + line.SCOPE.care + line.SCOPE.otherIncome + line.SCOPE.investments + line.SCOPE.retirement

SCOPE.residency.label: A nonresident or dual-status alien
SCOPE.residency.formula: if(person.residentAllYear, 0, unsupported("A nonresident or dual-status alien files Form 1040-NR or a dual-status return, which this app doesn't prepare")) + if(line.US.joint == 1, if(spouse.person.residentAllYear, 0, unsupported("Your spouse wasn't a U.S. citizen or resident alien all year: filing jointly then takes an election to treat them as a resident, which this app doesn't handle")), 0)

SCOPE.widowed.label: A spouse who died in 2025
SCOPE.widowed.formula: if(family.maritalStatus == "widowed", if(answer.spouseDiedIn2025, unsupported("Your spouse died in 2025, so you can file jointly for 2025; this app doesn't prepare that return yet"), 0), 0)

SCOPE.kiddie.label: A child's investment income taxed at the parent's rate
SCOPE.kiddie.formula: if(line.US.joint == 1, 0, if(person.age < 24 and line.US.unearnedIncome > param.kiddieThreshold, unsupported("Unearned income (interest, dividends, capital gains, pensions, taxable benefits) over $2,700 for someone under 24 may be taxed on Form 8615 (the kiddie tax), which this app doesn't prepare"), 0))
SCOPE.kiddie.source: Instructions, line 16, Form 8615: unearned income over $2,700; not for someone filing a joint return

US.unearnedIncome.label: Unearned income
US.unearnedIncome.formula: line.F1040.2b + line.F1040.3b + line.F1040.4b + line.F1040.5b + line.F1040.6b + max(0, line.F1040.7a)
US.unearnedIncome.source: Form 8615 instructions: unearned income is income other than earned income, such as taxable interest, dividends, capital gains, pensions and taxable social security benefits

SCOPE.otherIncome.label: Other income this app doesn't take yet
SCOPE.otherIncome.formula: if(answer.hasOtherIncome, unsupported("Other income (unemployment, rent, alimony, gambling and the like) isn't worked out yet: this return would leave it out"), 0) + if(line.US.joint == 1, if(spouse.answer.hasOtherIncome, unsupported("Your spouse has other income (unemployment, rent, alimony, gambling and the like), which isn't worked out yet"), 0), 0)

SCOPE.investments.label: Investment income this app doesn't take yet

SCOPE.retirement.label: Retirement income this app doesn't take yet

US.ownOrdinaryDividends.label: Ordinary dividends on this person's Forms 1099-DIV, box 1a

US.ownQualifiedDividends.label: Qualified dividends on this person's Forms 1099-DIV, box 1b

US.ownCapitalGainDistributions.label: Capital gain distributions on this person's Forms 1099-DIV, box 2a

US.ownReitDividends.label: Section 199A dividends on this person's Forms 1099-DIV, box 5

US.ownForeignTax.label: Foreign tax paid on this person's Forms 1099-DIV (box 7) and 1099-INT (box 6)

US.ownShortProceeds.label: Short-term proceeds on this person's 1099-B summaries for Form 8949 box A

US.ownShortCost.label: Short-term cost on this person's 1099-B summaries for Form 8949 box A

US.ownLongProceeds.label: Long-term proceeds on this person's 1099-B summaries for Form 8949 box D

US.ownLongCost.label: Long-term cost on this person's 1099-B summaries for Form 8949 box D

US.ownCarryoverShort.label: This person's short-term capital loss carryover

US.ownCarryoverLong.label: This person's long-term capital loss carryover

US.ownBrokerUnsupported.label: Sales this person's 1099-B summaries report that need Form 8949
US.ownBrokerUnsupported.formula: if(count(B.box1D) > countWhere(B.box1D, B.boxCAT, "A", "B", "D", "E"), unsupported("A 1099-B doesn't say which part of Form 8949 it is for (box A, B, D or E): enter it at Confirm"), if(countWhere(B.box1D, B.boxCAT, "B", "E") > 0, unsupported("Sales whose basis wasn't reported to the IRS (Form 8949 box B or E) go on Form 8949, which this app doesn't prepare yet"), 0))
US.ownBrokerUnsupported.source: Instructions, line 7a, Exception 2, and Schedule D, lines 1a and 8a: only sales with basis reported to the IRS and no adjustments go straight there

US.scheduleD.label: This return files Schedule D (1 for yes)
US.scheduleD.formula: if(line.US.ownBrokerSummaries + line.US.ownCarryoverShort + line.US.ownCarryoverLong + if(line.US.joint == 1, spouse.line.US.ownBrokerSummaries + spouse.line.US.ownCarryoverShort + spouse.line.US.ownCarryoverLong, 0) > 0, 1, 0)
US.scheduleD.source: Instructions, line 7a, Exception 1: no Schedule D when the only capital gains are capital gain distributions

SD.1ad.label: Short-term proceeds reported with basis (Form 8949 box A)

SD.1ah.label: Short-term gain or loss on line 1a

SD.7.label: Net short-term capital gain or loss

SD.8ad.label: Long-term proceeds reported with basis (Form 8949 box D)

SD.8ah.label: Long-term gain or loss on line 8a

SD.15.label: Net long-term capital gain or loss

SD.21.label: Capital loss deducted
SD.21.source: Schedule D, line 21: the smaller loss of line 16 or ($3,000), ($1,500) if married filing separately

F1040.7a.label: Capital gain or loss

hasHsa.ask: Contributions to a health savings account (HSA)
hasHsa.help: Money you put into an HSA yourself for 2025, not through your employer's payroll (that is in box 12 of your W-2, code W, and isn't deducted again). You need a high-deductible health plan (Form 8889).

hsaContributions.ask: HSA contributions you made yourself for 2025
hsaContributions.help: Including what you add by April 15, 2026 for 2025. Your HSA's Form 5498-SA shows them.

optionLabels.family: You and at least one other person (family coverage)

hsaAllYear.ask: Did the plan cover you in every month of 2025?

optionLabels.no: No, only part of the year

hsaNonMedical.ask: Did you take money out of the HSA for anything other than medical expenses?
hsaNonMedical.help: A Form 1099-SA shows distributions. Ones not for qualified medical expenses are taxed, with 20% more, on Form 8889.

hasIraContribution.help: Money you put into a traditional IRA for 2025, by April 15, 2026 (Schedule 1, line 20). Not a Roth IRA, and not a rollover.

iraContribution.help: Your IRA's Form 5498 shows them, or your statements if you contributed in 2026.

coveredByPlan.ask: An employer's retirement plan covered you in 2025
coveredByPlan.help: The "Retirement plan" box in box 13 of your W-2 is checked (a 401(k), 403(b), pension or the like). It can make your IRA deduction smaller.

paidForCare.ask: You paid for the care of a child under 13, or of a dependant who can't care for themselves, so you could work
paidForCare.help: Day care, a babysitter, before- or after-school care or a day camp in 2025, so you (and your spouse, filing jointly) could work or look for work. Not overnight camp, school from kindergarten up, or care by your spouse, the child's parent, your dependant or your child under 19 (Form 2441).

householdEmployer.ask: You paid a household employee, such as a nanny, $2,800 or more in 2025, or $1,000 or more in a calendar quarter of 2024 or 2025
householdEmployer.help: Someone who works in your home and does the work the way you tell them. You may owe household employment taxes on Schedule H.

priorYearCare.ask: You paid in 2025 for care given in 2024
priorYearCare.help: Care given in 2024 and paid for in 2025 can add to the 2025 credit (Form 2441, line 9b).

studentOrDisabledMonths.ask: Months of 2025 you were a full-time student or weren't able to care for yourself
studentOrDisabledMonths.help: Filing jointly, for each such month you are treated as earning at least $250 ($500 with two or more people in care), so the credit for child care can apply when one of you didn't work. Enter 0 if neither applies.

spouseNeedsCare.ask: Your spouse wasn't able to care for themselves, and you paid for their care
spouseNeedsCare.help: A spouse who can't dress, clean or feed themselves, or needs constant attention, and lived with you more than half of 2025.

cantCareForSelf.ask: Not able to care for themselves
cantCareForSelf.help: They can't dress, clean or feed themselves because of a physical or mental condition, or need constant attention to stay safe.

careExpenses.ask: Care you paid for them in 2025 so you could work
careExpenses.help: Paid in 2025 for care given in 2025, including what dependent care benefits from your employer paid. For a child who turned 13 in 2025, only care before their birthday. Not food, clothing, school from kindergarten up, or overnight camp.

careBenefitsCarriedOver.ask: Dependent care benefits from 2024 used in 2025's grace period
careBenefitsCarriedOver.help: Money left in a dependent care account at the end of 2024 that your employer let you use in early 2025 (Form 2441, line 13).

careBenefitsForfeited.ask: Dependent care benefits you lost or carried forward to 2026
careBenefitsForfeited.help: Money in a dependent care account for 2025 that you didn't use, because you had no care expenses for it (Form 2441, line 14).

optionLabels.child: Son, daughter, stepchild or adopted child
optionLabels.sibling: Brother, sister, half or step sibling
optionLabels.none: Not related, lived with you all year

monthsWithYou.ask: Months they lived with you in 2025
monthsWithYou.help: Count time away at school, in hospital or on vacation as time with you. For a child born or who died in 2025, count the months they were alive.

fullTimeStudent.ask: A full-time student in at least 5 months of 2025

paidOwnSupport.ask: Paid over half of their own support in 2025

filedJointReturn.help: Answer no if they file jointly only to get back tax withheld.

citizenOrResident.ask: A U.S. citizen, U.S. national or U.S. resident alien

grossIncome.help: Income that isn't exempt from tax, such as wages and interest; not social security benefits.

supportedByYou.ask: You paid over half of their support in 2025

hasSSN.ask: Has a social security number valid for employment
hasSSN.help: Issued by the due date of the return. The child tax credit needs one; without it, the credit for other dependents may apply.

claimedBy.help: Filing separately, each dependant is claimed on one spouse's return.

hasValidSSN.ask: You have a social security number valid for employment
hasValidSSN.help: Issued by the due date of the return. The child tax credit needs one (filing jointly, one spouse's is enough); the earned income credit needs one for you and, filing jointly, for your spouse; the deductions for tips and overtime need one for the person who received them.

paidHalfOfHome.ask: You paid over half the cost of keeping up your home in 2025
paidHalfOfHome.help: Rent or mortgage interest, property tax, utilities, repairs and food eaten at home. Head of household and qualifying surviving spouse need it, and so does the credit for child care when filing separately.

spouseDiedIn2023Or2024.help: With a dependent child who lived with you all year, you may file as a qualifying surviving spouse.

paidForEducation.ask: You paid for college or other higher education in 2025, for yourself or for a dependant
paidForEducation.help: Tuition and required fees for a university, college, vocational school or other school after high school that can take part in federal student aid. A Form 1098-T from the school shows what it received. It can give you the American opportunity credit or the lifetime learning credit (Form 8863). Each dependant's expenses are asked under their name.

educationExpenses.ask: Your own qualified education expenses in 2025
educationExpenses.help: Tuition and the fees and course materials the school requires, that you paid in 2025 for your own courses, less tax-free scholarships, grants and employer education aid. Start from box 1 of your Form 1098-T, less box 5. Not room and board, insurance, medical expenses or transportation. Enter 0 if you weren't a student.

educationCredit.help: The American opportunity credit is larger and partly refundable, but all of these must be true: the courses lead to a degree or other recognized credential; the student was enrolled at least half-time for at least one academic period that began in 2025; the student hadn't completed the first 4 years of college before 2025; the credit wasn't claimed for the student for 4 earlier years; and the student has no felony drug conviction. Otherwise, the lifetime learning credit counts any course at an eligible school, even one to improve job skills.

optionLabels.aotc: American opportunity credit (all of its conditions are true)

parentAlive.ask: At least one of your parents was alive at the end of 2025
parentAlive.help: With the American opportunity credit, someone under 24 who isn't filing jointly may get no refundable part of it (Form 8863, line 7).

fullTimeStudentSelf.ask: You were a full-time student in at least 5 months of 2025

earnedUnderHalfSupport.ask: Your earned income was less than half of your support in 2025
earnedUnderHalfSupport.help: Earned income is wages and self-employment income. Support is food, housing, clothing, medical care, education and the like, paid by you, your parents and others. A scholarship isn't support if you were a full-time student.

studentExpenses.ask: Qualified education expenses you paid for them in 2025
studentExpenses.help: Tuition and the fees and course materials the school requires, paid in 2025 by you or by them, less tax-free scholarships, grants and employer education aid. Start from box 1 of their Form 1098-T, less box 5. Not room and board. Enter 0 if they weren't a student after high school.

studentCredit.help: The American opportunity credit is larger and partly refundable, but all of these must be true: the courses lead to a degree or other recognized credential; the student was enrolled at least half-time for at least one academic period that began in 2025; the student hadn't completed the first 4 years of college before 2025; the credit wasn't claimed for the student for 4 earlier years; and the student has no felony drug conviction. Otherwise, the lifetime learning credit counts any course at an eligible school, even one to improve job skills.

optionLabels.aotc: American opportunity credit (all of its conditions are true)

hasStudentLoan.help: Interest you paid in 2025 on a loan taken out only to pay higher education expenses for you, your spouse or your dependant (Schedule 1, line 21). Your lender's Form 1098-E shows it. Filing separately, or if someone can claim you as a dependent, you can't deduct it.

studentLoanInterest.ask: Student loan interest not on a Form 1098-E
studentLoanInterest.help: Uploaded Forms 1098-E are added. Enter interest you paid in 2025 that isn't on one (a lender sends it only for $600 or more): the interest only, not the payments of the loan itself.

livedApartLastSixMonths.ask: You and your spouse lived apart for the last 6 months of 2025
livedApartLastSixMonths.help: Filing separately, you can get the earned income credit (with a qualifying child) or the credit for child care only if you didn't share a home with your spouse for the last 6 months of 2025.

hasDividends.help: A Form 1099-DIV from each fund, broker or company that paid you $10 or more of dividends or capital gain distributions.

hasBrokerSales.ask: Sales of stocks, bonds or funds
hasBrokerSales.help: A Form 1099-B from each broker. A broker's yearly statement usually sums the sales up by part of Form 8949 (box A, B, D or E): enter one 1099-B for each part, with its proceeds and cost.

hasLossCarryover.ask: A capital loss carried over from 2024
hasLossCarryover.help: A capital loss larger than the $3,000 ($1,500 filing separately) you could deduct in an earlier year carries over. Your 2024 Schedule D, or its Capital Loss Carryover Worksheet, shows it.

shortLossCarryover.help: Schedule D, line 6. Enter it as a positive amount.

longLossCarryover.help: Schedule D, line 14. Enter it as a positive amount.

hasItemized.help: Mortgage interest on your home, state and local taxes (income or property), gifts to charity and medical expenses (Schedule A). The app takes them instead of the standard deduction when they are larger. Your W-2s' state income tax (box 17) is counted for you.

itemMedical.help: What you paid in 2025 for medical and dental care, prescriptions and health insurance premiums for you and your family, less what insurance or anyone else paid back. Only the part over 7.5% of your AGI counts.

itemStateTax.ask: State and local income tax paid in 2025, not on a W-2
itemStateTax.help: Estimated state tax payments for 2025, and a balance you paid in 2025 for 2024. Box 17 of your W-2s is already counted.

itemRealEstateTax.help: Property tax you paid in 2025 on your home or land, yourself or through your lender (box 10 of a Form 1098 often shows it).

itemPersonalPropertyTax.help: A yearly tax based on the value of a car or boat, for example.

itemMortgageOther.ask: Mortgage interest not on a Form 1098
itemMortgageOther.help: Uploaded Forms 1098 are counted. Enter 0 unless you paid interest to a person rather than a lender.

mortgageQualifies.help: Each loan was taken out to buy, build or improve the home it is secured by (your main home or a second home), and all of them together are $750,000 or less ($375,000 filing separately; $1,000,000 for loans before December 16, 2017).

optionLabels.yes: Yes, both of these are true

itemCashGifts.ask: Gifts to charity by cash, check or card
itemCashGifts.help: To churches, schools, charities and other qualified organizations, with a receipt or bank record for each.

itemNoncashGifts.ask: Gifts to charity of things, not money
itemNoncashGifts.help: The fair market value of clothes, furniture or other things you gave. Over $500 in all needs Form 8283.

canBeClaimed.ask: Someone can claim you as a dependent
canBeClaimed.help: A parent or other person can claim you as a dependent on their 2025 return, even if they don't. Your standard deduction is then smaller (Form 1040, line 12a).

isBlind.help: Totally or partly blind on December 31, 2025, as a doctor certifies (Form 1040, line 12d). It adds to your standard deduction.

spouseItemizes.ask: Your spouse itemizes deductions on their separate return
spouseItemizes.help: When a married couple files separately and one of them itemizes on Schedule A, the other must itemize too (Form 1040, line 12b).

spouseDiedIn2025.help: A spouse who died during 2025 lets you file a joint return for 2025.

hasWages.help: A Form W-2 from each employer you worked for in 2025.

hasInterest.help: A Form 1099-INT from each bank, credit union or broker that paid you $10 or more of interest, and from the Treasury for savings bonds.

hasTipsOrOvertime.help: Tips you received in a tipped job, or overtime pay for hours over 40 a week. For 2025 you can deduct qualified tips and the "half" of time-and-a-half overtime on Schedule 1-A; filing separately, you can't.

hasOtherIncome.help: Income not asked above, such as unemployment compensation (Form 1099-G), a state tax refund that is taxable, rent or royalties (Schedule E), alimony, gambling winnings (Form W-2G), prizes, jury duty pay, a canceled debt, or income from a partnership, S corporation, estate or trust (Schedule K-1). This app doesn't take it yet: the return says so instead of leaving it out.

estimatedPayments.help: Estimated tax you paid for 2025, and any 2024 refund you applied to 2025 (Form 1040, line 26).

hasIraDistribution.help: A Form 1099-R from each IRA you took money out of, rolled over or converted, with the IRA/SEP/SIMPLE box checked.

hasPension.ask: Pensions, annuities or retirement plan distributions
hasPension.help: A Form 1099-R from each pension, annuity, 401(k), 403(b) or other plan that paid you, with the IRA/SEP/SIMPLE box not checked.

hasSocialSecurity.help: The Form SSA-1099 the Social Security Administration sends each January.

iraBasis.ask: You made nondeductible contributions to a traditional IRA (Form 8606)
iraBasis.help: Contributions you made in any year without deducting them are your basis: part of each distribution is then tax free, figured on Form 8606. Your earlier Forms 8606 show it. Most people answer No.

indirectRollover.ask: You put money from a distribution back into an IRA or plan yourself, within 60 days
indirectRollover.help: A rollover the payer didn't make for you (box 7 isn't G or H). The amount you put back isn't taxed, which this app doesn't work out yet.

earlyException.ask: An exception to the 10% additional tax applies to a distribution with code 1
earlyException.help: Code 1 in box 7 means you were under 59½. You owe 10% more on the taxable amount, unless an exception applies (such as disability, medical expenses over 7.5% of AGI, a first home up to $10,000 from an IRA, higher education from an IRA, or a separation from service in or after the year you turned 55). An exception is claimed on Form 5329, which this app doesn't prepare.

livedApartAllYear.ask: You and your spouse lived apart all of 2025
livedApartAllYear.help: Filing separately, more of your social security benefits are taxable if you lived with your spouse at any time in 2025 (Form 1040, line 6d).

qualifiedTips.help: Tips customers chose to give you, in cash or by card, in a job on the IRS's list of tipped occupations (such as wait staff, bartenders, hairdressers, delivery and rideshare drivers; see IRS.gov/TippedOccupations). Box 7 of your W-2 shows the tips you reported to your employer, and is the amount to start from. Not service charges or automatic gratuities. Enter 0 if your job isn't on the list.

qualifiedOvertime.help: Only the "half" of time-and-a-half that the Fair Labor Standards Act requires for hours over 40 a week, in a job that is not exempt from overtime. Your employer may show it in box 14 of your W-2 or on a statement. If you only know the total paid for your overtime hours at time-and-a-half, divide it by 3. Not pay above time-and-a-half, holiday or weekend premiums, or overtime paid under state rules only.

hasCarLoan.ask: Interest on a loan for a new car
hasCarLoan.help: Interest you paid in 2025 on a loan you took out after 2024 to buy a new car, minivan, van, SUV, pickup truck or motorcycle (Schedule 1-A, Part IV). A lease doesn't count.

carLoanInterest.ask: Interest you paid on the loan in 2025
carLoanInterest.help: The interest only, not the payments of the loan itself. Your lender's statement shows it.

carLoanQualifies.help: All of these are true: the car was new when you bought it (its first use started with you); its final assembly was in the United States (the label on the car, or the plant in its VIN, says so); you expect to use it for personal use more than half the time; and the loan is in your name and secured by a first lien on the car. You write the car's VIN on Schedule 1-A yourself.

optionLabels.yes: Yes, all of these are true

hasSelfEmployment.help: Income from your own business as a sole proprietor: freelancing, contract or gig work, a shop or a trade (Schedule C). A Form 1099-NEC, 1099-K or 1099-MISC often shows it. One business for each person.

businessIncome.help: Each Form 1099-NEC you add is counted. Enter everything else the business was paid in 2025: cash, cards, payment apps and platforms (a Form 1099-K), checks. Leave out sales tax you collected.

businessCar.help: The business part only: the standard mileage rate (70 cents a mile for 2025) times your business miles, or the business share of your actual costs, plus parking and tolls.

businessContractLabor.help: What you paid people who aren't your employees.

businessOffice.help: Postage, software subscriptions, stationery and other office costs.

businessRent.help: Rent for an office, a shop or a stall. Not for your home.

businessTravel.help: Business trips away from home overnight. Not meals, which are asked next.

businessMeals.help: The full cost; half of it is deducted.

businessUtilities.help: For business property, and the business part of your phone and internet.

businessOtherExpenses.help: Fees, bank charges, education for the business and other costs not above. List them in Part V of Schedule C.

businessExtras.ask: Anything else on your Schedule C

fileJointly.title: Filing jointly would cost you less
fileJointly.text: You and your spouse file separately. Filed jointly, as one return with both your incomes, the two of you would pay less, as worked out from what you entered. Filing separately keeps each of you liable only for your own return, but it gives up the earned income credit, the education credits, the student loan interest deduction and the tips and overtime deductions, and most of the child care credit. To file jointly, choose it on Personal info.

fileSeparately.title: Filing separately would cost you less
fileSeparately.text: Filed separately, each of you with your own return, the two of you would pay less, as worked out from what you entered, with both of you taking the standard deduction and every dependant on your return. Each of you is then liable only for your own return. To file separately, choose it on Personal info.

interestWithoutForm.title: Interest is taxable even without a 1099-INT
interestWithoutForm.text: A bank or credit union sends a Form 1099-INT only when it pays you $10 or more. Interest under that is still income. If you earned any, enter it as a 1099-INT on Income, from your account statements.

estimatedTaxPenalty.title: You may owe a penalty for paying too little during the year
estimatedTaxPenalty.text: You owe $1,000 or more, and more than a tenth of the tax shown on your return (line 24, less the refundable credits on lines 27a to 29). The IRS may then charge a penalty for not paying enough tax during the year, through withholding or estimated payments, unless an exception applies (for example, you paid at least your 2024 tax). This app doesn't work out the penalty (Form 2210): leave line 38 blank, and the IRS works it out and sends you a bill. To avoid it next year, have more withheld on Form W-4.

reading.documents: United States information returns (Forms W-2, 1099, 1098 and SSA-1099)
notes: Box numbers with a letter are written in capitals: box 1a of a 1099-DIV is 1A, box 2a of a 1099-R is 2A, box 1d of a 1099-B is 1D.

A W-2 prints boxes 1 to 20. Box 12 holds codes with amounts: report only the amount with code W, under 12W. Boxes 13 and 14 aren't read. The 'a' to 'f' boxes hold numbers, names and addresses, never amounts: leave them out.

On a 1099 or 1098, report the payer's, lender's or school's name as issuer. A form can print a box that is a checkbox (such as boxes 7, 8 and 9 of a 1098-T): leave checkboxes out, unless the list names one.

A Form 1099-R is type RIRA when its IRA/SEP/SIMPLE box is checked, and type R when it isn't. Its box 7 holds one or two distribution codes: report the first under 7 and a second, if any, under 7B (box 7 of 7D is 7, and D under 7B).

A broker's Form 1099-B usually comes as a yearly statement that sums the sales up by part of Form 8949: 'Box A' (short-term, basis reported to the IRS), 'Box B' (short-term, not reported), 'Box D' (long-term, reported), 'Box E' (long-term, not reported). Return one 1099-B for each part that has sales, with that letter under CAT and the part's totals: proceeds (1D), cost or other basis (1E), accrued market discount (1F) and wash sale loss disallowed (1G). Federal income tax withheld (box 4) goes on the first.
A broker's statement often holds a 1099-DIV and a 1099-INT too: return them as well.

For a Form 1098-T, person is the student, and issuer the school. For a Form 1098-E, person is the borrower, and issuer the lender. For a Form 1098, person is the borrower, and issuer the lender. For a Form SSA-1099, person is the beneficiary, and issuer is Social Security Administration.
A corrected form (marked CORRECTED) replaces the first one: read it like any other.
